第 25 章 Everyone Can Lead with Leverage每个人都可以用杠杆来领导

Steve Heller / 史蒂夫·赫勒

— 第 76 页 —

Leverage is an essential aspect of leadership whereby one's own work enables other people's work. Everyone can and should lead.

杠杆效应是领导力的一个重要方面——自己的工作能促进别人的工作。每个人都可以而且应该领导。

The glue that binds an effective team and organization is more than the group's collection of skills and knowledge; it consists of the ways we work together, and especially the ways in which we enable one another. When your effort enables and amplifies other people's work, you can be described as a multiplier, and your work exerts leverage. Tech leads and managers constantly enable their teammates; it's their job. For example:

绑定一个高效团队和组织的粘合剂不仅仅是团队的技能和知识集合；它包括我们一起工作的方式，尤其是我们互相促进的方式。当你的努力促进和放大了别人的工作时，你可以被称为乘数，你的工作发挥了杠杆效应。技术负责人和经理不断促进他们的队友；这是他们的工作。例如：

  • Projects need planning and ongoing facilitation to progress efficiently.项目需要计划和持续推进才能高效进展。
  • Individual contributors (ICs) need coaching to grow and become more effective.独立贡献者需要辅导来成长和变得更高效。
  • Teams need leadership to establish a productive environment and modes of collaboration.团队需要领导力来建立高效的环境和协作模式。

How ICs Can Exert LeverageIC 如何发挥杠杆效应

In addition to team leads and managers, colleagues who build tools and platforms also exert leverage as part of their jobs. All of these roles have natural leverage and enable an organization to operate efficiently.

除了团队负责人和经理，构建工具和平台的同事也在工作中发挥杠杆效应。所有这些角色都有天然的杠杆，让组织高效运作。

We can all do work that has leverage, enabling and multiplying the efforts of our colleagues. In fact, it is quite rare that an employee has broad impact or progresses to senior ranks with just expertise (depth) or perspective (breadth), or even both.

我们都可以做有杠杆效应的工作，促进和放大同事的努力。事实上，一个员工仅凭专业知识（深度）或视角（广度），甚至两者都有，就能产生广泛影响或晋升到高级别，是相当罕见的。

What might an individual contributor who is not a project lead do to exert leverage? Here are a few examples:

一个不是项目负责人的独立贡献者可以做什么来发挥杠杆效应？以下是几个例子：

— 第 77 页 —
  • Develop a tool, process, or method that makes your colleagues', as well as your own, work more efficient. Think of this as establishing a platform upon which colleagues can build.开发一个工具、流程或方法，让你同事和你自己的工作更高效。把它想成建立一个同事可以在其上构建的平台。
  • Generalize the root cause of an issue not only to prevent recurrence of the same problem, but an entire class of related problems, saving colleagues from correcting now-preventable issues.泛化一个问题的根因，不仅防止同一个问题复发，还防止一整类相关问题，让同事不用纠正现在本可以预防的问题。
  • When you learn, share your insight with others, multiplying the group's knowledge and making it more likely that your insight will find application.当你学到东西时，和别人分享你的见解，放大团队的知识，让你的见解更可能被应用。
  • The ability to step back and see the bigger picture is a valuable skill, both in designing and executing, especially when you can show others specific paths.退后一步看大局的能力是一项宝贵技能，在设计和执行中都如此，尤其是当你能向别人展示具体路径时。
  • These include validating requirements, design methodology, code quality, documentation, testing, success measurement, and reflection.包括验证需求、设计方法、代码质量、文档、测试、成功衡量和反思。

Communication Is an Essential Tool for Providing Leverage沟通是提供杠杆效应的重要工具

Effective communication, especially to groups, multiplies knowledge and is an essential task for a leader. This can be done through writing and presenting. Here are some tips:

有效的沟通，尤其是对群体的沟通，能放大知识，是领导者的重要任务。这可以通过写作和演示来实现。以下是一些技巧：

Know your audience. Consider what would be the correct technical level and the correct length of time for the particular audience. A given presentation might not be appropriate for two different groups. Radia Perlman, an excellent speaker, explains that the ability to speak at any level and for any length of time (with planning) requires both mastery of the material and the communication mode. This requires practice, and it is well worth the investment.

了解你的听众。考虑特定听众合适的技术深度和时长。同一个演示可能不适合两个不同的群体。优秀的演讲者 Radia Perlman 解释说，在任何深度和任何时长（有计划地）演讲的能力需要同时掌握材料和沟通模式。这需要练习，而且非常值得投资。

— 第 78 页 —

We are often communicating upward. Even though our managers are often familiar with the goals, usually you will be more of an expert in the subject at hand. That's why you're the one talking or writing. Be ready to dive deep because some leaders like asking chained sequences of questions. Ask a colleague if your audience is known for that sort of engagement. Do not hesitate to push back when the discussion wanders too far; time and topic management are appreciated by all.

我们经常向上沟通。即使我们的经理通常熟悉目标，你通常还是手头主题的专家。这就是为什么你在说或写。准备好深入，因为有些领导喜欢连环追问。问问同事你的听众是否以这种互动方式著称。当讨论偏得太远时不要犹豫反驳；时间和话题管理是所有人都欣赏的。

When you establish a regular channel of communication, a recurring report (upward), an organizational update (downward), and other vehicles, be clear about the goal of the channel, and be sensitive to the amount of time the recipient will typically allocate to each communiqué. It's better to state, "No major updates at this time" than to report unimportant progress.

当你建立一个固定沟通渠道——定期报告（向上）、组织更新（向下）和其他载体——时，明确渠道的目标，并敏感地注意接收者通常会花多少时间在每份公报上。说「目前没有重大更新」比报告不重要的进展要好。

When communicating with a mixed or broad audience, paint the picture first, and don't hesitate to deliver the conclusion at the start. Templates for meeting reports, conference reports, literature summaries, all while following an executive summary–first style, with a Highlights and Actions structure, permit the rapid digestion of the most salient points while at the same time allowing the reader an easy decision of whether to read on.

当与混合或广泛的听众沟通时，先画全貌，不要犹豫在开头就给出结论。会议报告、会议报告、文献总结的模板，都遵循执行摘要优先的风格，带亮点和行动结构，允许快速消化最突出的要点，同时让读者容易决定是否继续读。

Leverage, also known as scope or organizational impact, is commonly reflected in career ladders. For a manager or lead, we speak of scope of control, and for an IC, scope of influence.

杠杆效应，也称为范围或组织影响力，通常反映在职业阶梯中。对经理或负责人，我们说控制范围；对 IC，我们说影响范围。

To become and effectively serve as a leader, select work that exerts leverage, multiplying the effort of your colleagues. All leaders exert leverage, and doing leveraged work, by definition, makes you a leader.

要成为并有效服务于领导者角色，选择能发挥杠杆效应的工作，放大同事的努力。所有领导者都发挥杠杆效应，而做有杠杆效应的工作，从定义上说，就让你成为了领导者。
